question: Under MREC Rule 3.1(A), what is a responsible broker's duty with respect to the licensees licensed under that broker?
choice_a: To instruct them in the fundamentals of real estate practice, ethics of the profession, and the Mississippi Real Estate License Law, and to exercise supervision of their licensed real estate activities
choice_b: To instruct them in the fundamentals of real estate practice and professional ethics only, with supervision of active transactions left to each licensee
choice_c: To supervise only licensees who have been licensed for less than one year
choice_d: To delegate supervision to the office manager unless the broker objects in writing
explanation: MREC Rule 3.1(A) makes it the affirmative duty of the responsible broker to instruct affiliated licensees in real estate fundamentals, professional ethics, and the License Law, and to actively supervise the real estate activities for which a license is required. This duty is continuous and is not limited by a licensee's experience level or delegable to unlicensed staff.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(A)

question: A broker who is affiliated with, and operates under the supervision of, a responsible (principal) broker is prohibited from doing what under Rule 3.1(B)?
choice_a: Holding any license classification other than salesperson
choice_b: Acting independently as a broker at any time, or performing any real estate service without the full consent and knowledge of the employing or supervising broker
choice_c: Advertising property under the firm's name
choice_d: Receiving compensation directly from a buyer in a transaction
explanation: Rule 3.1(B) provides that a broker operating under a responsible broker's supervision must not act independently as a broker at any time, and the responsible broker remains liable for that affiliated broker's actions to the same extent as if the affiliated broker were a salesperson. The affiliated broker may not perform any real estate service without the full consent and knowledge of the supervising broker.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(B)

question: Under Rule 3.1(B), if a responsible broker agrees that an affiliated broker may perform certain real estate services outside the responsible broker's direct supervision, what must the responsible broker do?
choice_a: Nothing further is required as long as the arrangement is verbal
choice_b: Obtain approval from every other licensee in the office
choice_c: Notify the Commission in writing of the exact nature of the relationship and the names of the brokers involved, and again notify the Commission in writing upon termination of the relationship
choice_d: File a new branch office application
explanation: Rule 3.1(B) requires that when a responsible broker permits an affiliated broker to perform services outside the responsible broker's supervision, the responsible broker must notify the Commission in writing of the exact nature of the relationship and the identities of the brokers involved, and must again notify the Commission in writing when that relationship ends.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(B)

question: Per MREC Rule 3.1(F), what happens to the licenses of real estate licensees when their responsible broker's license expires, is suspended, or is revoked?
choice_a: They remain active but the licensees may not close any pending transactions
choice_b: The licensees automatically become responsible brokers themselves
choice_c: The Commission issues a 90-day grace period before any action is taken
choice_d: The licenses of every licensee then under that broker's supervision are automatically suspended, though a licensee may transfer to another responsible broker
explanation: Rule 3.1(F) states that the expiration, suspension, or revocation of a responsible broker's license automatically suspends the license of every real estate licensee then under that broker's supervision. Affected licensees may transfer to another responsible broker to resume active status.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(F); Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-35

question: Under MREC Rule 3.5, who must serve as Team Leader of an approved Real Estate Team or Group, and what supervisory relationship applies?
choice_a: A Broker Associate with at least one year of real estate experience, who has supervisory responsibility over team members while working under the supervision of the Principal Broker, and who may face discipline for team members' violations
choice_b: Any licensed salesperson chosen by the team, with no minimum experience required
choice_c: The Principal Broker personally, with no delegation permitted
choice_d: An unlicensed office administrator approved by the Commission
explanation: Rule 3.5(C) requires every team to appoint a Team Leader who is a Broker Associate with a minimum of one year of real estate experience. The Team Leader has supervisory responsibility over team members, operating under the Principal Broker's supervision, and can be subject to disciplinary action for violations of the License Law by team members under their supervision.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.5(C)

question: To qualify as a 'Real Estate Team or Group' under Rule 3.5(A), the participating active licensees must, among other requirements, work under the direct supervision of whom?
choice_a: A licensed attorney retained by the brokerage
choice_b: The same Principal Broker
choice_c: The Mississippi Real Estate Commission directly
choice_d: Any broker of their choosing, regardless of office affiliation
explanation: Rule 3.5(A) requires that to qualify as a Team or Group, the active licensees must, among other conditions, each work under the direct supervision of the same Principal Broker and conduct all real estate activity from the primary office or branch office where their individual licenses are displayed.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.5(A)

question: Under Rule 3.3(B), all advertising by licensees affiliated with a brokerage must be under whose direct supervision and must prominently display what?
choice_a: The direct supervision of the listing salesperson; the salesperson's cell phone number must be displayed
choice_b: The direct supervision of the Commission's advertising review office
choice_c: The direct supervision and in the name of the Principal Broker or Brokerage Firm, whose name must be conspicuous, discernible, and easily identifiable by the public
choice_d: No particular supervision is required if the advertisement is digital only
explanation: Rule 3.3(B) requires that all advertising be under the direct supervision of, and in the name of, the Principal Broker or the Brokerage Firm, and that the Principal Broker's or Firm's name be displayed conspicuously and be easily identifiable by a member of the public. This makes the Principal Broker directly accountable for advertising compliance firm-wide.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.3(B)

question: Rule 3.3(B) imposes what specific print-size requirement when a licensee's or team's name appears alongside the Broker's or Brokerage Firm's name in advertising?
choice_a: The licensee's or team's name must be printed larger than the Broker's or Firm's name
choice_b: There is no size requirement, only placement requirements
choice_c: Both names must use identical fonts but size is unregulated
choice_d: The Broker or Brokerage Firm must be identified using the same size or larger print than that used for a licensee, team member, or team
explanation: Rule 3.3(B) specifically requires the Principal Broker or Brokerage Firm to be identified in the same size or larger print than any licensee, team member, or team named in the same advertisement, reinforcing the broker's ultimate responsibility and visibility for firm advertising.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.3(B)

question: Under MREC Rule 3.2(G), how long must a real estate broker keep complete records relating to a real estate transaction on file?
choice_a: Three years following consummation
choice_b: One year following consummation
choice_c: Five years following consummation
choice_d: Indefinitely, with no defined retention period
explanation: Rule 3.2(G) requires a real estate broker to keep complete records relating to any real estate transaction on file for three years following the transaction's consummation. This retention duty supports the Commission's ability to audit and investigate broker recordkeeping.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(G)

question: Which of the following is explicitly listed under Rule 3.2(G) as part of the 'complete records relating to any real estate transaction' a broker must retain?
choice_a: Personal tax returns of the broker
choice_b: Listings, options, leases, offers to purchase, contracts of sale, escrow records, agency agreements, and copies of all closing statements
choice_c: Marketing budgets for the following fiscal year
choice_d: Only the final recorded deed
explanation: Rule 3.2(G) specifies (non-exhaustively) that the records a broker must retain include listings, options, leases, offers to purchase, contracts of sale, escrow records, agency agreements, and copies of all closing statements. This ensures a complete transaction trail is preserved.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.2(G)

question: Under Rule 3.4(C), what standard governs a broker's escrow account records, and who may inspect them?
choice_a: Records may be summarized annually and are inspected only upon a written complaint
choice_b: Only the broker's CPA may review escrow records, and the Commission must obtain a subpoena to inspect them
choice_c: Accurate records must be kept in accordance with standard accounting practices, with monies individually identified by transaction, and are subject to inspection at all times by the Commission
choice_d: Escrow records need only be kept for active listings, not closed transactions
explanation: Rule 3.4(C) requires accurate escrow account records covering all monies received, disbursed, or on hand, individually identified to a particular transaction, maintained per standard accounting practices, and subject to inspection at all times by the Commission — not merely upon complaint.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.4(C)

question: Under Rule 3.4(A), by when must a broker deposit earnest money into a trust account after acceptance of a mutually agreeable contract?
choice_a: Within 30 calendar days
choice_b: Only when the transaction closes
choice_c: Within five business days
choice_d: Prior to the close of business of the next banking day
explanation: Rule 3.4(A) requires that upon acceptance of a mutually agreeable contract, earnest money accepted by the broker (or by a licensee for whom the broker is responsible) must be deposited into a trust account prior to the close of business of the next banking day.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.4(A)

question: Under Rule 3.4(A), who bears responsibility at all times for earnest money deposits accepted by any licensee affiliated with the firm?
choice_a: The responsible broker, and the licensee must pay over all deposits and earnest money to the responsible broker immediately upon receipt
choice_b: The salesperson who personally accepted the funds, exclusively
choice_c: The buyer's lender
choice_d: Whichever party's attorney is handling the closing
explanation: Rule 3.4(A) makes the responsible broker responsible at all times for earnest money deposits handled within the firm. A licensee who personally accepts earnest money must pay it over to the responsible broker immediately upon receipt, reflecting the broker's non-delegable trust-fund accountability.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.4(A)

question: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-21(f) defines 'reasonable time' for a broker to account for or remit monies belonging to others (to avoid a disciplinary violation for failing to remit or for commingling) as what period?
choice_a: Ten calendar days
choice_b: The close of business of two banking days following the date the licensee or broker comes into possession of the monies
choice_c: Immediately, with no grace period
choice_d: The close of the calendar month
explanation: Section 73-35-21(f) defines 'reasonable time,' for purposes of the duty to account for and remit trust monies without commingling, as the close of business of two banking days following the date a licensee comes into possession of monies belonging to others (or a responsible broker takes or receives cash or checks from execution of an earnest money contract, option, or other contract). This is a distinct, disciplinary-code timing standard from Rule 3.4(A)'s next-banking-day deposit rule.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-21(1)(f)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-21(1)(f), which of the following is expressly listed as a ground for license suspension or revocation related to a broker's handling of other people's money?
choice_a: Charging a commission above the local average rate
choice_b: Refusing to accept a below-asking-price offer
choice_c: Failing, within a reasonable time, to account for or remit monies belonging to others, or commingling such monies with the broker's own funds
choice_d: Declining to represent a buyer without an exclusive agreement
explanation: Section 73-35-21(1)(f) lists, as a specific ground for refusing, suspending, or revoking a license, the failure to account for or remit within a reasonable time any monies belonging to others that come into the licensee's possession, or the commingling of such monies with the licensee's own funds.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-21(1)(f)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1), what must every person, partnership, association, or corporation licensed as a real estate broker have and maintain?
choice_a: A minimum of three affiliated salespersons
choice_b: A dedicated 24-hour answering service
choice_c: A separate corporate entity apart from any sole proprietorship activity
choice_d: A definite place of business — a room in the broker's home or an office elsewhere — used for transacting real estate business, which is designated in the license
explanation: Section 73-35-15(1) requires every licensed real estate broker to have and maintain a definite place of business — either a room in the broker's home or an office elsewhere — used for transacting real estate (or allied) business, and that location must be designated in the broker's license.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1), what must be prominently displayed in a broker's designated office?
choice_a: The certificate of registration of the broker and the certificate of each real estate salesperson employed by that broker
choice_b: Only the broker's personal photograph
choice_c: A copy of the Commission's annual budget
choice_d: Nothing is required to be displayed as long as records are kept off-site
explanation: Section 73-35-15(1) requires that the certificate of registration of the broker, and the certificate of each real estate salesperson employed by that broker, be prominently displayed in the designated office, giving the public and the Commission a visible record of who is licensed to operate from that location.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1)

question: If a broker relocates their designated office under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1), what notice must be given to the Commission?
choice_a: No notice is required if the new office is in the same county
choice_b: Application to the Commission must be made before removal, or within ten days after removal, designating the new office location
choice_c: Notice is only required if the broker changes firm names
choice_d: The broker has one full year to update the address on renewal
explanation: Section 73-35-15(1) requires a licensee relocating from the designated address to apply to the Commission before the move, or within ten days after the move, designating the new office location, after which the Commission issues a new license reflecting the new address for the unexpired license period.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(1)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(2), a real estate licensee must give the Commission written notice of a change of principal broker within how many days, and what happens if this notice is not given?
choice_a: Thirty days; the license is placed on probation
choice_b: Fifteen days; the licensee is fined $500
choice_c: Three days; failure to give notice automatically cancels the licensee's license
choice_d: No time limit is imposed as long as the change is eventually reported
explanation: Section 73-35-15(2) requires prompt written notice, within three days, to the Commission of any change of principal broker. A change of principal broker or employment without the required notice automatically cancels the licensee's license until it is reissued after proper acknowledgment.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-15(2)

question: Under MREC Rule 3.1(D), a responsible broker who operates more than one office must display what in each branch office, and what is the broker's resulting responsibility?
choice_a: A photocopy of the primary office's license is sufficient; no additional responsibility attaches
choice_b: Only a sign listing the branch manager's name
choice_c: Nothing additional, since branch offices are exempt from display requirements
choice_d: A branch office license in each branch office; the broker is responsible for the real estate practices of the licensees at each location
explanation: Rule 3.1(D) requires a responsible broker who maintains more than one office to display a branch office license in each branch office and confirms the broker remains responsible for the real estate practices of the licensees operating out of each of those offices, not just the main office.
source_note: MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 3, Rule 3.1(D)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-11, when a Mississippi broker enters a cooperative agreement with a broker licensed in another state who holds no Mississippi license, who is liable for the acts of the cooperating nonresident broker?
choice_a: The Mississippi broker is liable for all acts of the cooperating broker, as well as for the Mississippi broker's own acts, arising from execution of the cooperative agreement
choice_b: Neither broker is liable; liability rests solely with the salesperson involved
choice_c: The nonresident broker's home-state commission
choice_d: Liability is split 50/50 by statute regardless of fault
explanation: Section 73-35-11 provides that where a Mississippi broker cooperates with an out-of-state broker who is not Mississippi-licensed, the Mississippi broker must supervise the showing of and negotiations on Mississippi property and is liable for all acts of the cooperating nonresident broker, as well as the Mississippi broker's own acts, arising from execution of the cooperative agreement.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-11

question: Per the confirmed E&O insurance minimums applicable to active Mississippi real estate licensees under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(5), what per-claim and annual aggregate limits must the group policy meet, at minimum?
choice_a: A per-claim limit of not less than $50,000 and no aggregate requirement
choice_b: A per-claim limit of not less than $100,000 and an annual aggregate limit of not less than $100,000
choice_c: A per-claim limit of not less than $250,000 and an annual aggregate limit of not less than $500,000
choice_d: A per-claim limit of not less than $1,000,000 with no minimum aggregate
explanation: Section 73-35-16(5)(b)-(c) sets the minimum requirements for the group E&O policy issued to the Commission: a per-claim limit of not less than $100,000 and an annual aggregate limit of not less than $100,000. These same minimums also apply to independent coverage under § 73-35-16(7) and MREC Rule 9.3(B).
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(5)(b), (c)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(7) and MREC Rule 9.3(B), what are the maximum allowable deductibles for a licensee's independent E&O coverage?
choice_a: No more than $10,000 per claim regardless of type
choice_b: No deductible is permitted under any circumstances
choice_c: No more than $2,500 per licensee per claim for damages, and no more than $1,000 per licensee per claim for defense costs
choice_d: No more than $1,000 for damages and $2,500 for defense costs
explanation: Both § 73-35-16(7) and MREC Rule 9.3(B)(3) cap independent E&O coverage deductibles at not more than $2,500 per licensee per claim for damages, and not more than $1,000 per licensee per claim for defense costs. Reversing these figures, as in choice D, misstates the requirement.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(7)(c); MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 9, Rule 9.3(B)(3)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(5)(e), what happens to the mandatory E&O insurance requirement if the Commission is unable to obtain group coverage for all participating licensees at a premium of no more than a specified amount per 12-month policy period?
choice_a: The Commission must self-insure all licensees at no cost
choice_b: Licensees must each independently pay the difference
choice_c: The requirement is automatically extended for an additional year
choice_d: If the Commission cannot obtain coverage for all participating licensees at a premium of no more than $250.00 per twelve-month policy period, the insurance coverage requirement is void for that contract period
explanation: Section 73-35-16(5)(e) provides a safety valve: if the Commission cannot obtain group E&O coverage for all participating licensees at a premium of no more than $250.00 per twelve-month policy period, the statutory insurance coverage requirement becomes void for that contract period.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(5)(e)

question: Under Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(8)(a) and MREC Rule 9.2, what happens if a licensee fails to submit the required E&O premium or proof of independent coverage within 30 days of the applicable due date?
choice_a: The licensee is placed automatically on inactive status at the end of the 30-day period, and new licensees must provide proof within 30 days of licensure or face the same result
choice_b: The Commission automatically revokes the license with no further notice
choice_c: Nothing happens until the next renewal cycle
choice_d: The licensee is charged a one-time $5,000 penalty in lieu of coverage
explanation: MREC Rule 9.2(A) provides that active licensees who do not submit the required premium or acceptable proof of independent coverage within 30 days of the due date are automatically placed on inactive status at the end of that period, consistent with § 73-35-16(8)(a)'s requirement that new licensees furnish proof of E&O coverage within 30 days of licensure.
source_note: Miss. Code Ann. § 73-35-16(8)(a); MREC Rules and Regulations (rev. 2/21/2025), Part 1601 Ch. 9, Rule 9.2(A)
